title: Type A Affine Hecke Algebras and Bernstein PBW

items.title: The finite type-A Hecke basis over the multiplicative parameter ring
items.statement: Over R0=Z[Q,Q^-1], the finite type-A algebra with (T_i-Q)(T_i+1)=0 and the braid relations has basis {T_w}; this basis survives every commutative base change.
items.strategy: Extend scalars along Q↦v² to the free rank-two ring Z[v,v^-1], use T_i=vU_i and the generic standard basis, then reflect the resulting isomorphism through the faithful free extension.

items.title: The type-A weight lattice, Laurent ring, and divided differences
items.statement: For Λ=Z^n and A=Z[Q,Q^-1][X_1^±1,...,X_n^±1], adjacent transpositions act by variable swaps and D_i(f)=(f-s_i(f))/(1-X_i/X_{i+1}) is a well-defined Laurent polynomial with the twisted Leibniz rule.
items.strategy: Factor each swapped monomial through z^a-z^b and use finite geometric sums for all integer exponent differences, then extend by the Laurent monomial basis.

items.title: The rational skew group algebra for type A
items.statement: For K=Frac(A) with its S_n action, define finite sums Σ a_w[w] with (a[w])(b[v])=a w(b)[wv]; this is a unital associative R0-algebra with underlying K-vector space.
items.strategy: Extend each variable permutation to fractions and check associativity directly from the group action law.

items.title: The multiplicative Bernstein presentation of the affine Hecke algebra of type A
items.statement: Define the universal affine algebra over R0 by the multiplicative Hecke and type-A braid relations on T_i, commuting invertible X_j, and T_i f-s_i(f)T_i=(Q-1)D_i(f). The generator relations are equivalent to T_i X_i T_i=QX_{i+1} together with distant-variable commutation.
items.strategy: Construct the generator-and-relation quotient, extend generator cross-relations to Laurent monomials with the twisted Leibniz rule, and derive both forms of the compact Bernstein relation from the quadratic relation.

items.title: Demazure–Lusztig operators satisfy the affine type-A relations
items.statement: In K⋊S_n, T_i=Q[s_i]+(Q-1)(1-s_i)/(1-X_i/X_{i+1}) preserves A and satisfies the affine quadratic, braid, and Bernstein relations; its s_i coefficient is nonzero.
items.strategy: Construct K⋊S_n locally, compute quadratic and distant relations, and expand the six rank-three permutation coefficients for the adjacent braid using explicit rational identities.

items.title: Bernstein PBW basis for the affine Hecke algebra of type A
items.statement: The monomials X^λT_w form an R0-basis of the universal affine type-A Hecke algebra, and their scalar extensions form a basis over every commutative R0-algebra.
items.strategy: Rewrite Laurent variables to the left for spanning; use the nonzero leading permutation coefficient in K⋊S_n and a maximum-length argument for independence; then transport the universal free basis by base change.

items.title: The center of the universal affine Hecke algebra of type A
items.statement: Over R0, the center is A^S_n. The theorem makes no center-preservation claim for arbitrary specializations.
items.strategy: Commuting a central element with every X_j forces its skew-group support to fix all variables; the PBW leading term then leaves only A, and commuting with T_i forces S_n invariance.

title: Type A Affine Hecke Algebras and Bernstein PBW — Examples

items.title: A divided difference with negative Laurent exponents
items.strategy: Apply the variable transposition and multiply the claimed quotient by 1-X_1/X_2.

items.title: The rank-two multiplicative Bernstein relation
items.statement: For n=2, calculate both generator cross-relations and derive T_1X_1T_1=QX_2.
items.strategy: Evaluate D_1 on X_1 and X_2, substitute in Bernstein, and use the quadratic relation.

items.title: The rank-two polynomial-module action
items.statement: Compute T_1 on 1, X_1, and X_2 in the polynomial representation.
items.strategy: Use T_1(f)=Q s_1(f)+(Q-1)D_1(f) and the two generator divided differences.

items.title: Symmetric Laurent polynomials in the center
items.statement: The elementary symmetric polynomials are central, whereas X_1 is not.
items.strategy: Check invariance of the elementary symmetric sums and apply the universal center theorem.
